summary: quchip is an open-source Python toolkit that assembles device-independent simulations for superconducting quantum chips by explicitly representing device physics, control-line transformations, frames, approximations, dissipation, and observables. Using JAX-native dynamiqs, device and control parameters remain differentiable through time evolution, enabling forward prediction, correction via response-matrix inversion, and inverse parameter recovery from tomography.
motivation: Superconducting quantum chips require coordinating multiple layers—local Hamiltonians, control electronics, rotating frames, the rotating-wave approximation, noise channels, and measurement—making hand-assembled models brittle and hard to extend.
method: quchip organizes a chip as devices (Duffing transmons, resonators), couplings (capacitive interactions), and drives (charge lines with crosstalk). An engine resolves each device's reference frame to its dressed $0 \to 1$ frequency, decomposes operators into excitation-change bands to apply the RWA automatically, assembles collapse operators, and packs a differentiable problem for QuTiP or dynamiqs backends.
result: On a five-device model (two qubits, bus, two readout resonators), phase sweeps identified crosstalk phasors $0.16 e^{i 3.31}$ and $0.14 e^{i 1.885}$ between two charge lines; inverting the response matrix suppressed effective leakage by $>100\times$ and held corrected populations within 0.3 percentage points over sixteen simultaneous $\pi$ pulses. Adiabatic elimination reduced the Hilbert space from 576 to 16 dimensions; gradients through tomography recovered all four directed crosstalk parameters ($\beta_{12}, \theta_{12}, \beta_{21}, \theta_{21}$) with maximum complex error $1.5 \times 10^{-5}$.
